questions.question: Why do people start a SIP, and what do they expect to happen?
questions.headline: Among the 2,102 items that say why the person started, the most common reasons are long term wealth (43%) and specific goal (25%). Among the 1,524 that say what they expected, steady long term growth (74%) leads, followed by high or quick returns (14%) and safe like fd (8%).

stats.label: Stated reason for starting (n=2102 items that say why)
What they expect (n=1524 items that say)
Who influenced them (n=1302 items that say)

quotes.q: If I want to invest for 2 years, should I invest in RD or SIP mutual fund?. Which will give better return if I am not looking for a long time investment?
My investment horizon is 10+ years, and I'm comfortable with the volatility that comes with mid caps.
But it will secure your future and protect your wealth.
I feel India has a great future ahead, so doing sip in India is much better option
by investing in both I have some capital preserved and other is for aggressive growth

caveats: Only a minority of posts say why the person started or what they expected, so shares are among those who said.
Public posts skew to people who are already asking questions.

questions.question: What changes in their behaviour in the months after starting?
questions.headline: Among 1,101 items that describe a change after starting, paused or stopped (25%), stayed consistent (23%) and switched fund or platform (23%) lead. Items showing a drop-off signal make up 10% of 0-3 month posts, 16% of 3-12 month posts and 17% of 12+ month posts, but few posts state the stage, so treat this as a pattern to test.

stats.label: How behaviour changes after starting (n=1101 items that say)
What happens to the SIP, 0-3 months in (n=569)
What happens to the SIP, 3-12 months in (n=333)
What happens to the SIP, 12+ months in (n=1874)

questions.question: What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?
questions.headline: Among 512 drop-off signals that give a reason: understanding & expectation (43%), money or life event (27%), SIP broke (payment / mandate / app) (18%), pulled elsewhere (12%). Falling returns matter, but they are one reason among several.

stats.label: Stated reason among drop-off signals (n=512 that state one; 696 drop-offs in total)
Specific triggers
First-year only (n=94)

caveats: Reasons are only what people say publicly. Silent lapses are invisible, so their cause is unknown here.
Market falls are one trigger among several, not the whole story.

questions.question: What do investors check, and how often, once they have started?
questions.headline: Among 822 items that say what they look at, the most common are returns percent (32%), current value (30%), sip date status (14%). How often they look is stated in only 123 items (rarely (44%) lead), so frequency is indicative at best.

stats.label: What they say they look at (n=822 items that say)
How often they look (n=123 items that say)

questions.question: What separates investors who continue from those who quietly drop off?
questions.headline: Visible drop-offs show more confusion, anxiety or frustration than people who continue (62% vs 27%). Among those who state an expectation, 78% of continuing investors expect steady long-term growth, against 78% of drop-offs. People who lapse silently never appear in public text, so this contrast cannot show what separates them.

stats.label: People continuing (n=1998): where they go when unsure
Visible drop-offs (n=696): where they go when unsure
People continuing: what they check
Visible drop-offs: what they check
Continuing: feelings (n=1998)
Drop-offs: feelings (n=696)
Continuing: expectation stated
Drop-offs: expectation stated

questions.question: How do these patterns differ across user segments (income stability, age, source of money, who influenced them)?
questions.headline: Differences are small and rest on few items. Share showing a drop-off signal: irregular income 12.9% (n=70), variable pay 12.3% (n=65), fixed salary 9.0% (n=699). Only about 19% of items state income at all.

stats.label: Income stability: items that state it, and the share showing a drop-off signal
Who influenced them: items that state it, and the share showing a drop-off signal
Age band: items that state it, and the share showing a drop-off signal
Source of money: items that state it, and the share showing a drop-off signal

questions.question: What unmet needs emerge consistently across conversations?
questions.headline: Across 4,952 relevant items the biggest unmet needs are plain language explanation (16%), expectation setting (15%), reassurance whats normal (11%). Among first-year items: reassurance whats normal (17%), expectation setting (16%), plain language explanation (16%). Among drop-off signals: flexible pause or reduce (22%), reassurance whats normal (14%), plain language explanation (12%).

stats.label: All relevant items (n=4952)
First-year items (n=1063)
Drop-off signals (n=696)
